def matmul_flop_jit(inputs: List[Any], outputs: List[Any]) -> Number:
    """
    Count flops for the matmul operation.
    """
    # inputs should be a list of length 2 containing two tensors
    assert len(inputs) == 2, len(inputs)
    
    input_shapes = [get_shape(v) for v in inputs]
    shape_0 = input_shapes[0]
    shape_1 = input_shapes[1]
    
    # Handle different matmul cases
    # Case 1: Both 2D: (m, n) @ (n, p) -> m * n * p
    # Case 2: Both ND with batch: (..., m, n) @ (..., n, p) -> batch * m * n * p
    # Case 3: Mixed dimensions with broadcasting
    
    # Get the matrix dimensions
    # For shape_0: last dimension is n, second-to-last is m (or batch dims then m)
    # For shape_1: second-to-last dimension is n, last is p (or batch dims then n, p)
    
    m = shape_0[-2]
    n = shape_0[-1]
    p = shape_1[-1]
    
    # Calculate batch size (product of all dimensions except last 2)
    batch_size = 1
    
    # For shape_0, all dimensions except last 2 are batch dimensions
    for i in range(len(shape_0) - 2):
        batch_size *= shape_0[i]
    
    # For shape_1, we need to account for broadcasting
    # If shape_1 has fewer dimensions, it broadcasts
    # We need to match batch dimensions properly
    if len(shape_1) > 2:
        # shape_1 has batch dimensions
        batch_size_1 = 1
        for i in range(len(shape_1) - 2):
            batch_size_1 *= shape_1[i]
        # Take the maximum batch size (broadcasting)
        batch_size = max(batch_size, batch_size_1)
    
    flop = batch_size * m * n * p
    return flop
```
